Hi Olivia / James —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Recap (from discovery):
- Primary workloads: Chat-based clinical triage conversations + PDF summarization + embeddings for semantic search/reranking.
- Peak concurrent users: ~1,200 (US region), peaking M-F 09:00-18:00 PT.
- Typical request: chat context ~1.5 KB, response length ~150-300 tokens.
- Embedding throughput: batch embedding jobs overnight + ~30 qps for live search/rerank.

Open/required info:
1) Desired committed throughput (tokens/sec or qps) for SLA sizing.
2) Acceptable cold-start latency and max p95 latency SLO for chat.
3) Auth model: will you integrate with Redwood API keys, or do you need token exchange via your proxy?
4) Routing: Any requirement to pin traffic to specific regions or model variants for PHI workloads?
5) Embeddings/reranker placement: prefer co-located vs separate dedicated cluster?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ve attached an initial sizing workbook (dedicated_capacity_sizing.xlsx) and our rough network diagram (network_diagram_v1.png). Please review and fill the "Customer Inputs" tab with estimated qps, concurrency and retention windows.
- Schedule a 45-min technical alignment with our SE (Marissa) + infra engineer (Vivek) to finalize autoscaling & queueing approach.
- If you can, share a recent traffic snapshot (headers only) or a CSV with request timings — helps us validate batching assumptions.

Proposed times: Mon 2 Mar 10:00-10:45 PT or Tue 3 Mar 14:00-14:45 PT. Let me know which works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing & integration next steps

Hi team — quick technical note ahead of tomorrow’s sync. Below are our recommended defaults and rationale; we can walk through examples on the call.

1) Throughput and GPU sizing (high level)
- For chat generation using a decoder-only 8B-class model quantized to 4-bit on A100/RTX scale, expect ~1100-1500 tokens/sec per GPU under steady-state with batching (1-2k tokens per batch typical).
- If your average response is 250 tokens and average request includes 50 prompt tokens, a single GPU can handle ~4-6 qps of full-chat responses (depends on latency SLO).
- For p95 latency target ~600ms first token, we recommend sizing for lower batching (smaller batch windows) and adding 20-30% headroom.

2) Concurrency model & limits
- We enforce per-model-instance concurrency limits to avoid OOM and to maintain stable latency: default concurrent generation slots per model instance ~12 for chat on 8B optimized runtime.
- A "session" maps to a short-lived connection; long-running sessions should use prefix caching to avoid recomputing prompts.

3) Autoscaling & warm pools
- Dedicated pools support:
  - Warm standby GPUs (pre-warmed containers with model loaded): recommended for production-critical triage flows. Warm pools reduce cold-start from ~120s to ~5-10s.
  - Horizontal autoscaling: scale by instance count based on queued requests + CPU/GPU utilization signals. Typical scale step is 1-2 GPUs.
  - Policy suggestion: scale up when queue depth > 30 for 30s; scale down after utilization < 30% for 5m.

4) Queueing & backpressure
- Use a short in-memory request queue per routing shard; apply token-cost-aware prioritization (clinical triage > summarization > embeddings batch).
- Implement client-side retry with exponential backoff and jitter; honor Retry-After headers from Redwood.

5) Embeddings & reranker architecture
- Best practice is to run embeddings on a separate fleet: CPU-optimized nodes for small embedding models or dedicated GPUs for larger models.
- Live search/rerank at 30 qps: provision a small hot cluster (2-4 GPUs depending on model size) + nearline batch workers for bulk reindexing.

6) Auth & networking
- We support: API key, short-lived tokens via OIDC exchange (recommended for your gateway), and mTLS for private peered connections.
- For PHI, enable VPC peering + KMS key policy restriction. We will provide an allowlist of IP ranges and peering instructions.

7) Fallbacks & cost controls
- Route non-critical traffic to a cheaper model variant when utilization crosses a threshold. We can configure automatic fallbacks with rate limits.

Action items for tomorrow’s sync:
- Olivia/James: confirm committed baseline qps (you said 800 concurrent, but we need qps estimate).
- Aditya: confirm legal/contract lead time required for reserved capacity.
- Marissa: prepare a slide showing warm-pool vs cold-start tradeoffs and our recommended autoscaling policy.

If helpful, I’ve attached a sample sizing matrix and a short CLI example for token-exchange flow.
